analysis.title: Impartial analysis of Measure R

text: IMPARTIAL ANALYSIS OF MEASURE ITBDI
The California Constitution and Education Code authorize a school district to issue bonds for specified purposes if approved at an election by 55% of those voting on issuance of the bonds.

The Board of Trustees of the Burlingame Elementary School District (District) proposes this Measure, which would authorize the District to issue bonds in a principal amount not to exceed $100 million. The bonds will have an interest rate not exceeding the legal maximum and will be repaid within the time permitted by law. The Tax Rate Statement printed in this pamphlet contains the District's best estimates of tax rates required to service the bond debt during the life of the bonds, which is anticipated to last until June 2058. The District's best estimate of the average annual tax rate levy to fund this bond is $16.00 per $100,000 ($0.016/$100) of assessed valuation. The District estimates that the total amount repayable during the life of the bond, including principal and interest, will be approximately $195.5 million.

The California Constitution requires the listing of specific projects to be funded from the bond revenue and certification that the District Board of Trustees has evaluated safety, class size reduction, and information technology needs in the development of that list. The Bond Project List can be found in the full text of the Measure, and includes without limitation:

Construct, acquire, renovate, and equip classrooms, science labs, libraries, and other instructional facilities; Repair or replace leaky roofs, aging exterior walls, flooring, and ceilings; Replace aging and inefficient plumbing, electrical, and HVAC systems; Replace portable classrooms with permanent classrooms; Upgrade technology, computers, and network infrastructure; Upgrade security, fire, and safety systems, including security cameras and access controls; Complete accessibility improvements required by law; Repair, replace, or upgrade paved surfaces, parking, and outdoor facilities; and Make other repairs and improvements to modernize school facilities.

The Measure authorizes equipment acquisition, upgrades, repairs, services, construction, and other items related to the listed projects. The Bond Project List does not imply a specific prioritization among the projects, and should be reviewed for further details. 1351

No proceeds from the bonds shall be used for teacher or administrator salaries or other school operating expenses, except to reimburse the District for the cost of staff time spent working on the bond projects themselves.

State law requires that the District take certain steps to account for the proceeds from the bonds. Accordingly, the District will appoint an independent citizens' oversight committee, establish a special account for deposit of the bond proceeds, and conduct annual independent performance and financial audits to ensure that bond funds are spent only for the purposes listed in the Bond Project List and for no other purposes.

A "yes" vote on this Measure would authorize the District to issue bonds in a principal amount not to exceed $100 million for the purposes listed in the Bond Project List. [281 A "no" vote would prevent the District from issuing the bonds. [Ill This Measure passes if at least 55% of those voting on the Measure vote "yes."
End of Analysis (500 word limit. 489 words)

text: Vote Yes on _: Repair Burlingame schools to protect high-quality local education and keep local students safe. Burlingame Schools are at the heart of our community. For generations, we've delivered top-notch education to local students keeping both our schools and our community strong. But some of our schools are over 100 years old and their age is showing. Classrooms suffer from dry rot, leaky roofs, and outdated plumbing and electrical systems. We need to fix these problems now, so teachers have the tools they need and students can focus on learning in safe, modern classrooms ---— not on bursting pipes. Measure repairs our classrooms and labs so we can continue our tradition of academic excellence. Every local student deserves safe, modern facilities that set them up for success in high school, college, and beyond. Yes on : Repair Aging Local Schools Protect high-quality academic instruction in core subjects like math, science, reading, and writing Remove dry rot, lead, and asbestos Update science, technology, engineering, and math labs Fix leaky roofs Replace aging and inefficient plumbing and electrical systems Provide teachers with the tools to prepare students for high school and college

All Measure _ Funds Stay Local for Burlingame Schools • By law, all funds remain under local control and may only be used in Burlingame schools • No funds can be taken by the State or Federal government • An independent citizens' oversight committee and mandatory annual audits are required
Strong schools mean strong property values and a stronger community. Join parents, teachers, and neighbors across Burlingame in voting yes.
Yes on _ : Repair and Upgrade Local Schools

text: Argument Against Burlingame Elementary School District $97M Bond Issue: Measure In 2016 voters approved $56,000,000 in debt to "update classrooms" and in 2012 they approved $56,000,000 to "update classrooms". Now they want another $97,000,000 debt to do it all over again??? Do school classrooms really need upgrading every four years? Have they even spent the $56,000,000 from the 2016 bond or before? If not, why are they asking for. more of your hard-earned dollars? When bond debt measures like Measure are put before the voters, the school District is admitting that everything they are currently spending your tax dollars on now, is more important than the projects for which this tax increase is being sought. Budgets set priorities. Burlingame Elementary School District is saying every educational dollar spent today is going to a higher priority than to "renovate outdated classrooms". Do you agree? The District does not think "student safety" is important, because they are not in the current budget. Do you agree? The District does not think "leaky roofs" are important, because they are not in the current budget. Do you agree? Who takes out a 25-30-year loan to buy a personal computer? No one, right? But that is what the District did in 2012. You are paying for that now and will for decades to come, even though that technology became obsolete years ago. The website: www.ed-data.org shows 3,507 students in the district, which means this bond expense is $27,658 per student, plus 25-30 years of interest, plus $10,070 per student in the annual school budget. You deserved to know the full truth about the mountain of debt that is measure K. Reinember, financing school projects via bond debt, routinely doubles the cost of the project. And purchasing technology via bonds is nuts!
Just say No to more debt. Vote No on For more information: www.SVTaxpayers.org OFFICE OF THE ELECTiUNb MAR

text: This isn't the first time we've heard from this lone opponent of funding our schools. He doesn't live in the County, let alone our community. If he did, he'd know Burlingame's rich history of supporting local schools, making our community strong and such a special place to call home.
We feel obligated to set thc record straight and remind our neighbors why we need Measure R:

Some of Our Schools Are Over 100 Years Old. And their age is showing. Classrooms suffer from dry rot, leaky roofs, and outdated plumbing and electrical systems. Students are learning in outdated classrooms. Basic Repairs and Upgrades. Measure R removes hazardous materials like lead and asbestos, replaces aging pipes and roofing, and updates science, technology, engineering, and math labs, giving teachers the tools to prepare students for high school, college, and beyond. 100% of Funds Stay Local. By law, funds can only be used in Burlingame schools. No funds can be taken by the State or Federal Government. A Clear System of Accountability. An independent citizens' oversight committee and mandatory annual independent audits are required to make sure every penny is spent as voters intend.
Measure R keeps our tradition of academic excellence, protecting what makes Burlingame such a special place to live: strong schools, strong community, and strong students.
Let's make the essential, basic repairs and upgrades our schools need. Join teachers, small businesses, and community leaders — Vote Yes on Measure R!
RECEIVED
AUG 1 8
